These are mapped into a unified token set, ensuring semantic consistency. The kernel operates under the assumption that design systems must maintain a finite, ordered scale. Hardcoded values not conforming to this scale are flagged as outliers. Near-duplicates are identified via Euclidean distance in color space, enabling consolidation into a minimal token list. This process ensures scalability and reduces redundancy while preserving visual fidelity. Failure modes include misclassification of outliers due to insufficient variance thresholds or incorrect token hierarchy assumptions.
